scenario: AITA for having a photo of me with my friend’s girlfriend as my phone wallpaper? | I’m 23M. My friend Charley and I were tight back in college. We even lived together our second year. We’re still friends, but we kind of diverged. He found early success in his career and dating life, while I’m still single and doing entry level work. He started dating this model since last summer. I met her at a New Year’s party when Charley brought her. I knew about her since before Charley even started dating her. I follow a lot of models on Instagram and Charley’s girlfriend was one of them, but I wouldn’t call her a celebrity among the general public, especially in a city full of stars like LA. But anyways, I found her to be extremely pretty and introduced myself as a fan and asked her for a photo together. Charley took it. I respected their relationship and didn’t post that photo on social media, but rather used it as my phone wallpaper. She’s eye candy and it motivates me to work hard like Charley so hopefully one day I can call someone like her my girlfriend. She’s really sweet. Charley’s really lucky. I try my best to not be a creep around her or when discussing her with Charley. Yesterday, I had dinner with just Charley. We had a good time catching up. We didn’t talk much about his girlfriend until he noticed my phone wallpaper as we were waiting for the check. I wrote down a reminder to change that before meeting up with Charley yesterday, but I forgot about it. He asked me why I had that photo as my wallpaper. I was a little embarrassed and hesitated to speak for a few seconds. I just told Charley what I have already told him before, that I was a fan of her before they even started dating, but I respect their relationship and he doesn’t have anything to worry about. Charley never ridiculed me for not being good with women, but yesterday he told me that of course he doesn’t have to worry about me because a guy like me would never get a girl like her. He said he’d rather be the world’s biggest dickhead than be me. I was speechless. He started playing on his phone. Our bill arrived and it came to $63. I put down $40 and walked out. I still haven’t gotten an apology from Charley.
